currentContext.business: Following the demerger of the Lifestyle business (to Raymond Lifestyle Limited) and the Real Estate business (to Raymond Realty Limited), Raymond Limited now holds its Engineering business through majority-owned subsidiaries JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (Precision Technology & Auto Components, Tools & Hardware) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (Aerospace & Defence), and its Denim business through a 50% joint venture, Raymond UCO Denim Private Limited. The group supplies precision-engineered automotive, industrial and aero-engine components to domestic and global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers; at the standalone Raymond Limited level, the Company's own disclosed turnover comes from Aviation and Investment activities.

currentContext.strengths: Market leadership in Ring Gears and Steel Files segments in India|Long-standing relationships (2+ decades) with leading global aerospace OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, supported by high entry barriers and stringent qualification requirements|Positioned as a Global 'Tier 1.5' aerospace partner offering one-stop-shop capabilities across machining, assembly and specialised processes, combined with competitive 'best cost country' manufacturing|Diversified engineering portfolio across Precision Technology, Auto Components, Tools & Hardware and Aerospace & Defence, reducing dependence on any single industry segment|Export-led model with presence across 65+ export countries and 18+ global customer locations|Aerospace order book exceeding INR 2,350 crore over the next five years, providing revenue visibility
currentContext.strategies: Multi-horizon planning framework — a 10-year vision, a 5-year strategic roadmap, and a detailed Annual Operating Plan (AOP) driving execution, reviewed through defined KPIs and monthly/quarterly reviews.|Growth primarily driven through organic initiatives, underpinned by continuous innovation.|Balanced, portfolio-led approach to the EV transition rather than a binary shift — building hybrid-component exposure while its core four-wheeler and commercial-vehicle exposure transitions gradually.|Customer-led demand visibility — deepen participation across existing and new customer programmes, RFQ pipelines and confirmed order visibility, and increase share of business with existing OEMs and Tier-1 partners.|Shift towards higher value-added, precision-engineered components and deeper co-design/assembly integration with customer platforms to enhance margin profile.|Geographic diversification and global exposure to reduce concentration risk and participate in global supply chains.|Driving Industry 4.0 / digitalisation integration across operations, including real-time monitoring of machine performance (OEE).|Positioned as a Global 'Tier 1.5' aerospace partner, deepening programme participation (e.g. LEAP engine programme, casting programmes, new product categories such as vanes) and expanding into new geographies (UK, Belgium, Sweden).|Deepening share of wallet with top-10 OEM customers via Just-in-Time (JIT) warehousing established in the US and Europe.
currentContext.expansion: Raymond Limited, through its subsidiaries JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (JKMPTL) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (JKMGAL), is progressing a new aerospace manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh — a ₹510 crore investment designed to produce high-precision aero-engine parts for leading global OEMs — alongside a new ₹430 crore automotive component facility at Gudipalli positioned within India's evolving EV supply chain, together a combined ~₹1,000 crore capital allocation committed to support multi-year backlogs. During FY2026 the Aerospace & Defence segment was described as 'progressing steadily' on the Andhra Pradesh expansion project with planned long-term capacity addition. JKMPTL was formed by unifying the erstwhile Tools & Hardware business, Ring Plus Aqua Limited and the auto business of Maini Precision Products Limited into a single integrated platform and now operates 15 integrated manufacturing facilities; separately, the Company's Precision Technology & Auto Components / Tools & Hardware operations comprise 16 manufacturing facilities across 4 locations in India (Nashik, Vapi, Chiplun, Bengaluru), supported by 1,800+ machines and 11 global 3PL warehouses.
currentContext.mdna: India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies in FY2025-26, supported by strong domestic demand, infrastructure spending and improving manufacturing activity; real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% (FY2026-27 projected at 6.6%).|Indian precision engineering market is expected to grow from USD 536 million (2025) to USD 996 million by 2034, driven by automation, smart manufacturing and localisation initiatives.|Auto components demand remains strong across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and tractors, supported by infrastructure spend, rural cash flows and increasing localisation/EV-hybrid adoption; commercial vehicle EV penetration nearly doubled to 1.83% and passenger vehicle EV share rose to 4.25% in FY26.|India aerospace & defence market is expected to reach nearly USD 54.4 billion by 2033 (CAGR ~8.1%), driven by defence modernisation, indigenisation and rising aircraft demand.|EV adoption is segment-specific, skewed towards two-wheelers, while the Group's core four-wheeler/commercial-vehicle exposure is expected to transition more gradually towards hybrid powertrains; ~10% of revenues are already linked to hybrid components with a roadmap for further scaling, and a further ~10% of revenues come from non-automotive segments (hydraulics, industrial, locomotive, marine, power tools).|In flexplates, the domestic market is estimated at ~0.6-0.65 million units annually with realisations of ~₹565-570 per unit; in ring gears, annual production exceeds 10 million units, with demand supported by low BEV penetration and continued reliance on ring gears even in mild-hybrid vehicles.|Aerospace segment revenue is highly export-oriented (~79% from exports); LEAP engine programme contributed ~₹110 crore (Apr 2025-Feb 2026), legacy CFM56 programme ~₹1.5 crore and other programmes ~₹20 crore, with the portfolio mix shifting towards more complex LEAP components.|Commercial aviation represents ~86% of the aerospace segment mix, complemented by defence and other segments, giving a balanced and resilient portfolio.|Aerospace & Defence order book exceeding INR 2,350 crore over the next five years.|LEAP engine programme contribution of ~₹110 crore (Apr 2025-Feb 2026), with legacy CFM56 (~₹1.5 crore) and other programmes (~₹20 crore) continuing to contribute, and the portfolio mix shifting toward more complex LEAP components.|Secured nominations for multiple components and assemblies from a European advanced drivetrain technology company.

risks.note: The Company's aerospace and auto-component businesses remain sensitive to global demand cycles, economic slowdowns and geopolitical uncertainties, which may impact order inflows and profitability.

Raymond is undertaking significant investments towards capacity expansion (Andhra Pradesh and Gudipalli facilities) and advanced manufacturing facilities, which may temporarily exert pressure on operations.

risks.risk: Margin pressure from input cost volatility
risks.note: Fluctuations in prices of aerospace-grade metals and raw materials may affect operating margins, particularly during periods of supply chain disruption and inflationary pressure.
Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, trade disruptions and logistics bottlenecks may impact raw material availability, exports and operational efficiency across global markets.
The engineering and aerospace sectors remain highly competitive, with global players continuously investing in technology, innovation and cost efficiencies.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance challenges in Aerospace & Defence
risks.note: Aerospace and defence businesses are subject to stringent certifications, quality standards and regulatory approvals, which may lead to operational or project execution risks if not managed effectively.

risks.risk: Long product qualification and approval cycles
risks.note: The aerospace business involves long product qualification and approval cycles, while evolving customer requirements in EVs, aerospace and precision engineering necessitate continuous investment in technology, quality systems and manufacturing capabilities.

risks.risk: Demand volatility in key export markets
risks.note: The Company remains exposed to global trade uncertainties and demand volatility across key export markets, particularly Europe, and the automotive and aerospace sectors, compounded by supply chain disruptions and raw-material price fluctuations affecting delivery schedules and costs.

one-line thesis: Raymond's engineering arm delivered resilient double-digit growth in Aerospace (26% FY26) and margin expansion in Auto (13.4% vs 11%), driven by global OEM diversification and operational synergies, while guiding for a transformative INR930cr capex to double capacity via a new Andhra facility by late FY28. The shift from 'build-to-print' to 'build-to-spec' and a record order book provide multi-year visibility despite near-term raw material import dependencies.
financial scorecard: Consol Revenue INR2,312cr (+10% YoY); EBITDA INR335cr (flat YoY) with margin compression to 14.5% (vs 15.9% FY25) primarily due to loss of INR600cr non-operating interest income post-Realty demerger cash transfer, not operational decay; PAT impacted similarly by non-operating shift. Aerospace Rev INR392cr (+26%), EBITDA INR88cr (+25%), Margin 22.3% (stable). Auto Rev INR1,667cr (+10%), EBITDA INR223cr (+34%), Margin 13.4% (up from 11%), boosted by INR13cr one-time land sale gain in Q2 and SAP-driven synergies. Order book robust at INR2,350cr (Aerospace). Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash INR68cr).
guidance: Revenue CAGR ~25% for Aerospace over next 2 years; Auto margins sustainable at ~13-14% excluding one-offs; Order inflow steady with 250-350 new SKUs/year; Capex INR930cr over 5 years (INR500cr Aero, INR430cr Auto); New Andhra facility commissioning late CY2027 (Q4 FY28) contributing meaningful revenue from FY29.
order book & pipeline: INR2,350cr (Aerospace specific); >10-year visibility on global aircraft backlog; 75% of book tied to engine programs across multiple OEMs (derisked from single platform); RFQ pipeline converting to multi-year contracts.
segment / subsidiary detail: Aerospace (JKMGL): Rev INR119cr Q4 (+11%), Margin 25.5%; Full Year Rev INR392cr (+26%), Margin 22.3%. Auto/Precision (JKMPT): Rev INR442cr Q4 (+5%), Margin 15.2%; Full Year Rev INR1,667cr (+10%), Margin 13.4% (incl. INR13cr one-off). Corporate: Neutral/Even-steven.
growth verticals / optionality: Migration to 'build-to-spec' (design ownership) vs traditional 'build-to-print'; Expansion into aerostructures, landing gear, and hydraulics (currently 25% of mix); Gas turbine segment exploration; 300-350 new components added annually; Andhra greenfield facility enabling 2x capacity scale.
margins & cost dynamics: Aerospace margins stable at 22-25% despite 100% imported raw materials (Titanium, Inconel); Auto margins expanded 240bps FYoY due to operational synergies, SAP integration, and product mix, partially aided by INR13cr land gain; Near-term pressure expected from raw material inflation but pass-through mechanisms active; Localization of raw materials (6-8 month timeline) identified as key future margin lever.
capex / expansion: Total INR930cr over 5 years; INR500cr allocated to Aerospace (scaling engine/structural capacity); INR430cr to Auto/Precision; Annual run-rate ~INR200cr (INR100cr per subsidiary) for FY27-28; Fully funded via internal accruals and existing cash, no parent equity infusion required for organic growth.
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet with INR68cr net cash (consol) and ~INR1,000cr liquid investments at parent; Capex self-funded by subsidiary cash flows; Parent liquidity acts as safety net; No dividend specifics given but strong cash generation supports potential payouts.
risks & watch-items: 100% reliance on imported aerospace-grade raw materials (supply chain/geopolitical risk); Execution risk on Andhra facility timeline (late FY28); Global OEM certification delays; Potential lag in passing through raw material cost inflation; Concentration in engine components (75%) though diversified across OEMs.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'derisking' customer base and moving up value chain; Transparent about one-offs (land gain, interest income shift); Modular growth approach to capex (machinery ordered quarterly based on ramp-up) rather than big-bang; Long-term optimism on India's role in global aerospace supply chain.
non-obvious takeaways: The flat consolidated EBITDA is an accounting artifact of the Realty demerger (loss of interest income on INR600cr cash transfer), masking a actual ~20% operational EBITDA growth; The company is transitioning from a job-shop model to a 'co-design' partner (build-to-spec), which fundamentally changes valuation multiples; Machinery procurement is continuous and modular (every quarter) to match SKU ramp-up, avoiding large single-point capex risks.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global OEMs face supply chain friction and need derisked, certified Tier 1 partners in India for engine and structural components. | Raymond Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of China+1 and global aerospace backlog; unique 'build-to-spec' capability and 25% CAGR guidance with visible order book. |
| Rising input costs and logistics blockades impact margins for companies reliant on imported specialty alloys. | Unorganized Precision Machining Peers | loser | Med | Companies without long-term OEM contracts or localization roadmaps will suffer margin compression; Raymond's scale and localization plans provide a moat. |

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
